findings.summary: The BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.CREATED notice WH-S7ACO2ASBYMD1T6BP-2KM9T49HQCR6YGFQT was accepted without checking its signature (on 2026-11-01). Anyone who can reach your webhook URL could send a notice like it.
findings.explanation: Your app acted on a notice without checking that PayPal really sent it. Anyone who finds your webhook address could send a fake "payment completed" or "cancelled" and your app would believe it.
findings.fix: Call PayPal's verify-webhook-signature endpoint before trusting a notice, and reject it unless the answer is SUCCESS.

Leo still had access from 2027-01-01 to 2027-01-15 although PayPal had suspended the subscription (2 checks).
findings.explanation: Your app's idea of whether this customer has access disagreed with the subscription's real status at PayPal. Usually the app ignored a suspend or cancel notice, or handled notices out of order.
findings.fix: Set access from the subscription status every time a notice arrives, and handle suspended, cancelled and expired as well as activated.

findings.summary: Maya was given what they paid for 2 times from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-20, but only 1 payment had completed (2 checks). Something was delivered without a matching payment, for example a repeated notice handled twice.
findings.explanation: PayPal sent the same notice twice and your app treated it as two payments, so the customer got the product twice for one charge. PayPal may deliver a notice more than once, by design.
findings.fix: Remember the id of every notice you have handled and ignore any id you have seen before.

Dispute PP-D-39784 opened on 2026-11-20 was not answered by the deadline of 2026-12-10. PayPal rules for the customer when the seller stays silent.
findings.explanation: A customer opened a dispute and your app did not respond before the due date. When the seller stays silent PayPal decides in the buyer's favour and you lose the money.
findings.fix: When a dispute-created notice arrives, send your evidence (for example tracking details) through the disputes API, or alert a person before the due date.
